mstts:express-as.prosody: Building a Life and Ministry While Wrestling with the Past. You know, adulthood doesn’t usually announce itself with some big, dramatic entrance. Most of the time, it just sort of sneaks in—one choice at a time. Some decisions you make intentionally, others you make just to get by. If you’ve grown up in a complicated family or fought to hang on to your faith, stepping into independence can feel both thrilling and a little terrifying. There’s this deep desire to start fresh, to build something meaningful that isn’t just a replay of old hurts. Marriage adds a whole new layer. Suddenly, it’s not just your story anymore—it’s two lives, two histories, trying to create a home together. There are these amazing moments: shared dreams, inside jokes, the comfort of knowing someone really gets you. But let’s be real—the past has a funny way of showing up, even when you think you’ve left it behind. Old fears, old habits…sometimes you find yourself reacting in ways you never expected. Work, especially if you’re teaching, leading, or serving in the church, can become a lifeline. There’s real purpose in helping others, seeing lives change, and making a difference. That sense of meaning is powerful. But, the pressure? It’s real. The need to have it all together—especially in public—can feel overwhelming. You might look like the confident leader on the outside, but inside, those old insecurities can still whisper in your ear. There’s this constant tension between public ministry and private pain. On stage, it’s all about hope, healing, and redemption. But behind the scenes, life is just…messier. Some days, faith feels stretched thin. The expectations, both from others and yourself, can get heavy. It’s tempting to put on a brave face and act like everything’s fine. But here’s something to pay attention to—over time, you realize that being real matters way more than being perfect. People connect with honesty, not just polished answers. When you open up about your doubts, your failures, those nights when you wondered if you’d make it through…that’s when real connection happens. It’s risky, sure, but it’s also incredibly freeing. Community makes all the difference. Trusted friends, wise mentors who don’t judge, and a spouse who sticks with you through the storms—these are the people who help you keep going. Healing isn’t instant. It comes in small, steady steps. And looking back? It’s clear—the past didn’t just leave scars. It actually became the ground where empathy and resilience could take root. Ministry stops being about having all the answers, and becomes more about walking alongside others as they wrestle with their own struggles. The journey’s still going, but there’s a deeper peace growing—a sense that even the most tangled-up lives can find redemption.
